note: English study material for post 02, kept OUT of the blog (Kunhao, 2026-10-25). C1 and C2 only. Levels are AI4Read estimates in the style of the English Vocabulary Profile, not an official grading. Example sentences restate ideas from the post; claims that are our reading say so.

items.sentence: Don't conflate algorithmic trading with AI trading: many algorithms follow simple rules.
items.definition: to treat two different things as if they were the same

items.sentence: Models trained on the same data may move in lockstep.
items.definition: moving or changing together, at exactly the same time and in the same way

items.sentence: One shared model can become a single point of failure.
items.definition: one part of a system whose failure stops or harms the whole system

items.sentence: Institutions are held accountable for the AI systems they deploy.
items.definition: to be made responsible for something and required to explain it or bear its consequences

items.sentence: Most participants in the IMF's outreach want a human in the loop in any AI-based strategy.
items.definition: a person who must check or approve what an automated system does before it takes effect

items.sentence: For Searle, collective acceptance confers on a printed piece of paper the status of money.
items.definition: to give someone or something an official status, right or quality

items.sentence: On Searle's account, money is underpinned by continued collective acceptance.
items.definition: to be supported or made possible by something that lies beneath it

items.sentence: Accountability presupposes someone who can be asked why.
items.definition: to need something to be true or to exist already in order to work or make sense

items.sentence: Responsibility cannot simply devolve onto a system that cannot be punished, so it falls on whoever deploys it.
items.definition: (of a duty or responsibility) to pass to someone else

items.sentence: If many firms chase the same signal, their trades may compound a shock rather than absorb it.
items.definition: to make a problem or difficulty worse by adding to it

items.sentence: Imposing one standard menu of contracts can be at odds with Haldane and May's call for diversity.
items.definition: to disagree with or not match something

items.sentence: Whether a machine-only token is money hinges on whether machines can do the accepting.
items.definition: to depend completely on one particular thing

items.sentence: Standard contracts cut both ways: they make checking easier, but they make firms more alike.
items.definition: to have both good and bad effects, or to support both sides of an argument

items.sentence: Every firm on one model? That’s a big if.
items.definition: used to say that a condition is very uncertain

items.headword: to read too much into something
items.sentence: Don’t read too much into a toy with ten banks.
items.definition: to think something has more meaning or importance than it really has

items.sentence: The toy helps, with the caveat that its numbers are invented.
items.definition: with the warning or limitation that

items.headword: what remains to be seen is whether
items.sentence: What remains to be seen is whether machines can do the accepting.
items.target: What remains to be seen is whether
items.definition: used to introduce a question that has not been answered yet

items.sentence: Running a market is by no means the same as answering for it.
items.definition: not at all; certainly not

items.sentence: The IMF judges that the risks currently appear contained; the FSB warns that common models could correlate trading; Gensler and Bailey hypothesise a monoculture.
items.definition: Choose the reporting verb to match how firm the source is: judge, warn, hypothesise, argue, concede.

items.sentence: It is declaring and answering, not running, that make a group of people a society, on our reading.
items.definition: Put the new or important information between 'It is … that' to control where the listener's attention falls.

items.sentence: Were every firm to rely on one model, their errors would be likely to coincide.
items.definition: A formal way to state an unlikely condition: 'Were X to do Y, …' instead of 'If X did Y, …'.

items.sentence: Rarely does a single toy settle a question about real markets.
items.definition: After 'rarely', 'seldom', 'not until' or 'only when' at the start of a clause, put the auxiliary before the subject. Formal writing and talks.

items.sentence: The five jobs comprise running, deciding, checking, declaring and answering.
items.wrong: The five jobs comprise of running, deciding, checking, declaring and answering.
items.right: The five jobs comprise running, deciding, checking, declaring and answering.
items.definition: 'Comprise' takes a direct object; use 'consist of' if you want 'of'.

items.sentence: Shared models could make failures coincide.
items.wrong: Shared models could possibly perhaps make failures coincide.
items.right: Shared models could make failures coincide.
items.definition: One well-chosen hedge is enough; piling up 'could', 'possibly' and 'perhaps' sounds unsure rather than careful.

items.sentence: The survey implies that most managers are cautious; from it we infer that deciding is still mostly human.
items.wrong: From the survey we imply that deciding is still mostly human.
items.right: From the survey we infer that deciding is still mostly human.
items.definition: Evidence or a speaker implies (suggests); a reader or listener infers (concludes).

items.sentence: Having automated the checker, we face a new question: who checks it?
items.wrong: Having automated the checker, a new question arises: who checks it?
items.right: Having automated the checker, we face a new question: who checks it?
items.definition: An opening participle phrase must describe the subject that follows; a question cannot automate a checker.

items.sentence: Cover the expression, read the definition and the sentence with a gap, and say the expression aloud before you check. Recognising an expression is not the same as being able to use it.
Pick a system you know (a journal, a lab, an online community) and describe in two minutes who runs, decides, checks, declares and answers, using three expressions from this pack.

loop.text: Software already runs much of the market, but running is by no means the same as answering for it. Were many firms to rely on one model, their errors would be likely to move in lockstep, and that model could become a single point of failure. Most participants in the IMF's outreach want a human in the loop, partly because accountability presupposes someone who can be asked why. A token counts as money only while a community keeps accepting it, so whether a machine-only token is money hinges on whether machines can do the accepting, and what remains to be seen is whether they ever could. Standard contracts cut both ways: they make checking easier, yet they make firms more alike. We should not read too much into a toy with ten banks, with the caveat that it shows what could happen, not what will.
